accuracy.evidence: Checked against the KS3 programme of study (probability: 'use the language of ... equally likely outcomes', record outcomes of experiments) and CCSS 7.SP.C.7a (uniform probability model). Every number recomputed: three 120° slices = 1/3 each; 2 of 6 equal sections = 1/3; 3 red : 1 blue gives red three times as likely; 6 of the 36 ordered pairs total 7 (1+6 … 6+1) and 1 pair totals 2 or 12; loaded dice P(6) = 1/3 with 2/15 for each other face. The seeded 60-roll runs were enumerated: fair dice A (seed 4) gives 8, 8, 12, 10, 11, 11; loaded dice B (seed 16) gives 7, 9, 9, 9, 6, 20 sixes. Parameterised answers (r − b, n, k − 6, n) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the equiprobability bias documented by Lecoutre (1992) (two outcomes therefore 50-50: win/lose, snow/no snow, totals 2 to 12 all equal), counting colour names instead of equal sections, the belief that a 6 is harder to roll (Amir & Williams 1999), the gambler's-fallacy 'dice remembers' slip, and expecting exactly 10 of each in 60 rolls. Wrong card sorts, wrong two-dice taps (e.g. 3 + 5 = 8), accusing the fair dice and each wrong challenge answer get a message naming that slip.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed; the highest 6-token Jaccard is 9.4% (shared shell scaffolding with flag_varx.js). 533 Likelihood language (flaglikely) paints counters to match chance words, 105 Probability as a fraction takes equal likelihood as given, and 619 Simple chance experiments tallies one coin. Only this lab drags a spinner's edges to equalise slices, recolours equal sections so three colours share them, taps the 36 red/blue dice pairs for 7, and tests a fair dice against a seeded loaded one.

lab_teaches.evidence: The five tasks build the idea in order: equal-sized sections give equal chances; equal sections still need an equal share per outcome; ask whether anything favours an outcome (six sorted situations); the number of outcomes is not the chance (6 of 36 pairs make 7, 1 makes 2); when you cannot see inside, test many times, and fair results wobble round equal. Each banner states the rule only after the learner's own drags or taps reach it.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Yes, always: there are 3 colours' for a three-colour spinner, 'Yes: there are two outcomes' for win or lose, 'Yes: every total is equally likely' for 2 versus 7 with two dice, and 'Exactly 10' or 'Fewer than 5, because 6 is hard to roll' for 60 fair rolls. The spinner drag, the card sort, the 36-pair grid and the 60 seeded rolls then disprove each one.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each with two tagged wrong answers: countNames (red, red, blue, yellow spinner), sixRare and memory (dice), bigBetter and allTotals (two-dice totals), luckyPlace and oneTry (5 green, 5 purple), exact (60 rolls) and twoWays (rain or not). Every tag has its own message, e.g. 'A dice has no memory. Each roll starts fresh, so after three 6s a 6 is still 1 in 6.'

readability.evidence: Kid explanation Flesch-Kincaid grade 4.5 (limit 6.5) and adult 8.3 (limit 9.5), checked with learn/readability.py. Sentences are short and concrete (coins, dice, bags of counters, a team's match), and 'equally likely' is defined in the first kid sentence before it is used.

no_filler.evidence: No filler patterns matched. Every kid paragraph carries one idea with a worked example (fair dice; equal sections; 3 red 1 blue; 36 pairs and testing). The adult text gives curriculum links, the exact lab sequence and named misconceptions. Explanation overlap with every other lesson is at most 0.4%.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px (iPhone-size, both themes) and 1200 px desktop for all six steps before and after Show me: the spinner, six-section wheel, 7×7 dice grid and two tally panels fit with no clipping after reserving footer space (spinner radius and grid size now leave room for a three-line message). Spinner handles have a 28 px grab radius, grid cells are about 44 px on phone, and the two sort boxes are full-width halves.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag and tap has a button twin: edge ◀/▶ buttons, one button per section, Equally likely / Not equally likely, one button per pair making 7, Roll ×10 then 'Dice B is unfair'. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with section sizes, colours, pairs found or roll counts. walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop or iPhone 13, with no console errors.
